summary: Gold Ridge's 1930s crow's nest was still standing in the 1980s per the register; Willhite found a rock platform outline and phone-line insulators near the summit.

facts.design: Crow's nest, described as the only structure on the ridge
facts.status_note: Crow's nest still standing in the 1980s per the register and Kresek inventory; firelookout.com lists it as gone; Willhite reports a rock platform outline and phone-line insulators near the summit

access.note: National Forest land; Willhite describes a paved access road and an off-trail climb

visit.trail_note: Per Willhite: from the paved Gold Creek Road, the Oxide Canyon road is faint and off trail in places; the country is mostly open

events.note: Crow's nest built in the 1930s; sources give only the decade (decade-level precision)
firelookout.com says abandoned in the 1930s (decade-level precision)
Crow's nest still there in the 1980s per the register and the Kresek inventory (decade-level precision)
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, April 9, 2020; nominated by Tammy McLeod

corrections.why: The register's Built field reads 1930's, which is a decade. No source gives the exact year 1930.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com put the site at 4,200 feet; Willhite puts the probable summit site at 4,585 feet. The story reports both.
firelookout.com says abandoned in the 1930s; the register and the Kresek inventory say it was still standing in the 1980s. Both are reported and not reconciled.
The register's photo caption gives 11-4-1939; Willhite gives November 4, 1938 for the ground panoramas. The panoramas are not part of the story.

notes_for_editor: The brief's coordinates from firelookout.com (48.22834, -120.18119) do not appear in the page text that was fetched, so they are not cited. The register gives 48.223987, -120.191486. Willhite's summit placement is his inference ('appears to have been placed'), and the story says so. The access level 'public' is inferred from National Forest land and Willhite's road description, not stated outright; the editor may prefer to drop it. Willhite's separate panoramic-site page (gold_ridge_panoramic/images_338.htm) was not read.
